question.text: Fixed Maturity Plans (FMPs) are particularly suitable in which interest rate environment, and why?

answer.text: Falling interest rate environment, because bond prices rise
Rising interest rate environment, because investors can lock into high yields
Stable interest rate environment, because there's no reinvestment risk
Any environment, because FMPs guarantee returns

explanation.text: The Logic: FMPs are preferred in a rising interest-rate environment because investors can lock into the high prevailing yields. Since FMPs hold the underlying securities passively until maturity, interest-rate (price) risk is eliminated when the investor stays invested until maturity. The Trap: FMPs do not guarantee returns — they eliminate interest-rate risk only when held passively until maturity. Credit risk on the underlying securities still remains. Note: The yield benefit comes from locking in current high yields; focus on the hold-to-maturity yield lock-in when assessing suitability.
